advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either include the actual patch (drop `--stat` or add `-p`/`--patch`) or correct every 'diff' reference to say 'diffstat/summary' so the prompt matches what is prefetched.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:311-314 `"show", "--stat", "--format=%H%n%s%n", sha,`
docstring line 284: 'Best-effort ``{sha: diff_text}`` ... referencing-commit diffs'
completion_verifier.md new paragraph: 'the file bodies (and any referencing-commit diffs) pre-loaded'
`git show --stat` documented behavior: prints a diffstat and suppresses the textual patch
advisory.finding: referencing_commit_diffs invokes `git show --stat --format=%H%n%s%n <sha>`; `--stat` suppresses the patch and emits only a diffstat summary + commit subject, yet the module docstring, function docstring, PrefetchSpec docs, gate_ops comment, and the verifier prompt all describe the prefetched content as referencing-commit 'diffs'. No actual diff/patch text is ever prefetched.
advisory.suggested_fix: If diffs are intended, replace `--stat` with `-p --stat` (or `--patch`) subject to the 4000-char cap; otherwise rename the accessor and update the docstrings/prompt to say 'diffstat'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only skeleton-compress .py bodies; for oversize non-Python files, head-truncate with a marker (or leave the raw clamp) instead of running Python-signature skeletonization.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:119-120 `if len(body) > per_file_char_cap or body.count("\n") + 1 > SKELETON_LINE_THRESHOLD:` then `skeleton_compress(body)` unconditionally
_is_signature_line only recognizes `def `/`async def `/`class `/`@` (completion_prefetch.py:167-173)
_normalize_impact accepts any declared path (no .py filter) — a ticket may declare .md/.yaml/.json in file_impact
advisory.finding: clamp_and_format applies skeleton_compress — which only preserves Python `def`/`class`/`@`/docstring lines — to ANY body over per_file_char_cap or SKELETON_LINE_THRESHOLD, regardless of language. A large non-Python file_impact file (Markdown, YAML, JSON, a big config) has no signature lines, so skeletonization collapses nearly the entire body to elision markers, prefetching almost no usable content while still labelling it 'skeleton'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Gate skeleton_compress on `path.endswith('.py')`; for oversize non-.py bodies, truncate to the char cap with an explicit 'call read_file for the rest' marker.

advisory.suggested_fix: Either add a diff format flag (e.g. drop `--stat` or add `-p`/unified diff) so real diffs are captured, or change the docs to say "referencing-commit diffstats/summaries" to match the `--stat` output.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route completion_prefetch._read_body through the same _safe_path(root, path, denied)/denied_paths envelope the agentic read_file uses so ticket-declared file_impact paths cannot escape the repo root or read denied internal-state paths.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:329-335 `_read_body`: `full = os.path.join(str(repo_root), path)` then `open(full, ...)` with no confinement or deny check
pai_tools.py:54 the agentic tool guards every read: `target = _safe_path(root, path, denied)`
fs_tools.py:27-31 `_safe_path`: refuses `path escapes the repository root` AND raises for `_is_denied(abs_path, denied)`
config.py:300-306 `denied_paths` = realpaths of `.git`, `.bridge_state`, `.tickets-tracker`, tracker_dir — 'Realpaths the agent must never read OR cite ... so neither can leak internal state'
leaf.py:176-182 `_validate_json_array` validates only that each `path` is a string — no traversal/deny validation, so file_impact path values are untrusted
operations.py pre-story path (lines 106-124) rendered only ticket description/comments — no file bodies were read from disk before this change, so the arbitrary-path disk read is newly introduced
advisory.finding: completion_prefetch._read_body reads ticket-declared file_impact paths from disk with a raw os.path.join(repo_root, path)+open(), enforcing NEITHER the repo-root traversal guard NOR the security deny-list that the agentic read_file tool enforces, so a ticket whose file_impact points at .git/, the tracker/event store, or an ../ traversal target gets those contents read and injected into the verifier LLM context.
scenarios: A ticket (agent- or user-authored) declares file_impact path `.git/config` or `../../etc/passwd` or a path under the tracker/event store; the close-gate prefetch reads it and embeds the bytes in the verifier context, exfiltrating denied internal state or out-of-tree files the read tool would have refused.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _read_body (and _discover_test_globs match resolution), resolve each path with rebar.llm.fs_tools._safe_path(root, path, denied_paths(root)) and skip (return None) on ValueError, so traversal and deny-listed paths are refused exactly as the read_file tool refuses them.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Account for the 2-char '\n\n' separator in fit_within_ceiling's budget (or pass the joined-length overhead in) so base + sep + fitted cannot exceed physical_context_ceiling.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:217 `budget = ceiling - len(base_context)`
gate_ops.py:167 `context = base + ("\n\n" + fitted if fitted else "")`
completion_recovery.py:164 `if len(context) > context_ceiling:` raises `CompletionRecoveryError('completion recovery context bound exceeded')`
fit_within_ceiling docstring: 'NEVER returns something that overflows the ceiling' — but the +2 separator added by the caller is outside its accounting
dropped.finding: fit_within_ceiling sizes the prefetch so len(base)+len(returned) <= ceiling, but gate_ops concatenates `base + "\n\n" + fitted`, adding a 2-char separator that is never counted; a maximally-fit prefetch produces a context of ceiling+2 chars, which trips `_validate_recovery_inputs`'s `len(context) > context_ceiling` refusal — the precise 'oversize prefetch is trimmed, not raised' guarantee the docstrings claim to uphold.
dropped.suggested_fix: Reserve the separator in the budget, e.g. pass `len(base_context) + 2` as the effective base length (or subtract the join length from `budget`) so the returned section plus the '\n\n' the gate adds stays <= ceiling.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Require a path-separator (or full-segment) boundary in fetch_overlap's suffix match so 'foobar.py' does not count as covering declared 'bar.py'.
evidence: usage_log.py:336 `if any(target == dp or target.endswith(dp) or dp.endswith(target) for dp in declared):`
docstring: 'matches a declared path by EXACT path or by one being a SUFFIX of the other' — a bare string suffix, not a path-component suffix
dropped.finding: fetch_overlap's suffix match `target.endswith(dp) or dp.endswith(target)` has no path-separator boundary, so unrelated files with a shared trailing substring count as covered — e.g. read target 'foobar.py' matches declared 'bar.py', and any read of 'x.py' matches a declared 'x.py' anywhere. This over-counts the coverage fraction the AC and the live A/B analysis report on.
dropped.suggested_fix: Guard the suffix branch with a boundary check, e.g. treat `a` as a suffix of `b` only when `b.endswith('/' + a)` (plus the exact-equality case).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Regex-escape ticket_id (re.escape) before embedding it in the git `-P --grep` pattern in referencing_commit_diffs.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:294-295 `"-P", f"--grep=(^|\\b){ticket_id}\\b"` — ticket_id embedded raw into a PCRE grep pattern
completion_prefetch.py:300 `subprocess.run(grep_args, ... )` is list-form (shell=False) so this is NOT command injection
assemble_prefetch passes `canonical = ticket.get("ticket_id", spec.ticket_id)` into referencing_commit_diffs — a ticket-state-derived value
dropped.finding: referencing_commit_diffs interpolates the ticket-derived ticket_id directly into a git `-P` (PCRE) `--grep` regex pattern, so a crafted ticket_id becomes attacker-influenced regex; while shell=False prevents command injection, the value is an unescaped regex metacharacter sink passed to git's PCRE engine.
scenarios: A ticket_id containing PCRE metacharacters alters which commits match (over- or under-matching) or forces a costly regex on git's grep; contained to the read-only git log and the whole helper is fail-open, so impact is limited to prefetch content selection rather than execution.
dropped.suggested_fix: Build the grep pattern from `re.escape(ticket_id)`, e.g. `f"--grep=(^|\\b){re.escape(ticket_id)}\\b"`.
